title: Consecutive Characters
spaceBreakdown:
- int cur, maxPower: two scalars → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion
- not counted: input string s
approach: Scan the string once, maintaining the length of the current run of identical consecutive characters. When `s[i] != s[i-1]`, reset the run length to 1; otherwise increment it. Track the maximum run length seen. Correctness: any single-character substring is exactly a contiguous run of that character, so the longest such run is the answer.
hints: If you walk through the string once from left to right, what single comparison tells you that the current run of identical characters has just ended?
Linear scan with a running counter. For "abbccc": compare each `s[i]` with `s[i-1]` - b==b makes the run 2, then c≠b resets to 1, then c==c→2, c==c→3; the max seen is 3.

**Single character** - smallest valid input, loop body never executes.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `best = 0` and only updating it inside the loop → returns `0`.

**All equal** - every position extends the same run.
`Input: s = "aaaa"` → `Expected: 4`
⚠️ Bug: resetting `cur = 1` before updating `best` → returns `3`.

**Max run at the very end** - the longest run is the suffix.
`Input: s = "abbb"` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: updating `best` only when the character changes → returns `1`, since the final run never triggers an update.

followUps.q: The string arrives as a streaming character feed you cannot store. How do you compute the power?
followUps.a: Keep only the previous character and the current run length plus the running maximum. Each new char is compared to the previous one, updating the count or resetting it. Time stays O(n), space drops to O(1) with no string stored.

followUps.q: Return every character that achieves the maximum power (not just the length).
followUps.a: During the same scan, whenever `cur` equals the current `best`, add `s[i]` to a result set; when `cur` exceeds `best`, clear the set and insert `s[i]`. Time O(n), space O(1) since at most 26 lowercase letters can be stored.

followUps.q: You may change up to k characters to any lowercase letter; find the maximum achievable power.
followUps.a: This becomes the "longest substring with at most k replacements" problem: use a sliding window with a frequency map, expanding the right end and shrinking the left while `window_size - max_freq > k`. Time O(n), space O(1) (26 letters).
